# Payment Process Clause

Provides payment-instruction-local request actions and an optional conditional capture policy. Configured workflows or document rules propose actions; only the guarantor's instruction operations confirm financial outcomes. An action result of `acceptedNew` means a new request or local change was recorded, not that money moved.

All paths refer to the document containing this clause, including a payment instruction's own document when embedded elsewhere.

## Capture policy

`parameters.method` defaults to `reservation`; supported values are `reservation`, `card` and `myos-customer`. The payment request functions independently check `/paymentTerms/method`, with the same default and supported values.

`parameters.capture` defaults to an empty object. Its `mode` defaults to `workflow`, which installs the configured action connections without adding a conditional capture gate. Mode `when` requires a `when` expression and a nonempty `requestId`.

In `when` mode, the clause installs `/paymentProcess_{clauseKey}/captureAllowed`, initially false, and sets `/paymentTerms/captureGate` to that path. An existing different capture gate is rejected. The gate becomes true only when `/activation/active` is true, the predicate evaluates exactly to true, and—if `/clauses/documentSources` exists—`/sourceLinks/ready` is true. It is reevaluated on changes to `/payment`, `/activation`, `/sourceLinks` and the predicate's static document dependencies, with an additional embedded-node handler when `parameters.sources` is nonempty.

Predicates permit static `$document` reads, comparisons, Boolean operations, existence, membership, size, addition, subtraction and literals. `$nodeBlueId` requires a direct static `$document` read. Dynamic or root paths, unsupported operators, undeclared `/sources/<alias>` reads and excessive nesting are rejected; aliases must appear in `parameters.sources`.

When the gate permits capture, the automatic step checks acceptance, transaction attachment, an open instruction, an unlocked capture action, no pending cancellation, sufficient unreserved secured funds, any required recipient approval, and absence of its configured request ID. It then requests exactly `/paymentTerms/amountMinor`. The native request function still checks recipient selection, target limits and other financial guards. The automatic amount does not adjust to the remaining balance or a resolved final target, and an existing request ID prevents automatic reissue even after a failed request.

Every new capture request, including a workflow request, checks the instruction's configured capture gate. A true gate establishes neither available funds nor a confirmed capture. Later gate changes do not cancel recorded requests or prevent their guarantor outcomes. The clause's transition hook rejects changes with `PAYMENT_PROCESS_POLICY_IMMUTABLE`.

## Request actions

- `requestAuthorize` requests `secure`; `requestCapture` requests `capture`. Both default `amountMinor` to `/paymentTerms/amountMinor`.
- `requestRefund` requests `refund` and has no amount default here. `requestVoid` requests release of the entire remaining authorization; its amount defaults to the recorded amount on replay, otherwise current `secured`.
- Financial input uses `amount` when supplied, otherwise `amountMinor`. Amounts are integer minor units of `/paymentTerms/currency`, positive and at most 1,000,000,000,000; a void may be zero.
- `requestPayeeAssignment` proposes an allowed `payeeRef`. `requestTransactionDetailsUpdate` proposes an object in `transactionDetails`. `requestFinalAmountResolution` proposes an integer `finalAmount` from zero through `/paymentTerms/limitMinor`.
- `requestPaymentCompletionLock` and `requestPaymentCompletionUnlock` propose capture-lock changes. `requestPaymentReversalLock` and `requestPaymentReversalUnlock` propose refund-lock changes. `requestTransactionDetailsUpdateLock` and `requestTransactionDetailsUpdateUnlock` propose details-lock changes.
- `approveRecipient` records approval only through a workflow whose calling channel equals the currently selected, nonempty `/payment/payeeChannel`. Repeated approval makes no new change.

Requests require a nonempty `requestId` without `/` or `~`, supplied through the configured mapping or caller input. Request `reason` defaults to empty text. Reusing an identifier with identical intent records no new request; conflicting intent or reuse across financial and control requests is rejected. Calling an exposed action does not establish a personal obligation or the current reader's authority.

## Financial state and decisions

These actions use `/paymentTerms` and the instruction's `/payment` ledger. Ledger initialization requires a positive integer `amountMinor`, an integer `limitMinor` at least that amount and no greater than 1,000,000,000,000, nonempty `currency`, Boolean `recipientApprovalRequired`, declared payer and guarantor channels, and a list of declared `allowedPayees`. An optional initial `payeeChannel` defaults to empty and, when selected, must be allowed.

Initialization starts financial amounts and reservations at zero, lifecycle and approval flags at false, locks unlocked, `transactionId` empty and `targetMinor` equal to `amountMinor`, then requests guarantor acceptance. These defaults apply only after initialization; missing state is unknown.

A new financial request requires an accepted instruction and an attached transaction. Closed instructions allow refunds but reject further secure, capture and void requests. Capture and refund obey their respective guarantor locks. Pending cancellation blocks new secure and capture requests.

Securing capacity accounts for completed captures, remaining secured funds and outstanding secure reservations against `targetMinor`. Capture requires a selected payee, recipient approval when required, sufficient secured funds after capture and void reservations, and room under the target after completed and reserved captures. Refund capacity excludes successful refunds and outstanding refund reservations from completed captures. Void requires no outstanding secure, capture or void reservation and releases the entire remaining authorization. A zero-amount void can still be pending, so `cancellationPending` carries information that `reserved.void` alone cannot express.

New financial requests enter `/payment/requests` with `status: pending` and reserve capacity under `/payment/reserved`. The guarantor reports `succeeded`, `declined`, `failed` or `unknown`, correlated by request ID and action. Optional amount assertions must equal the recorded request amount; non-success outcomes require a nonempty reason. `unknown` remains unresolved and retains its reservation. A terminal outcome releases the reservation; only success changes confirmed financial amounts. Identical responses are duplicates, conflicting terminal responses are rejected, and an unknown result can subsequently be reconciled.

`secured` is the remaining confirmed authorization: successful securing increases it, capture reduces it, and successful void clears it. `completed` is cumulative successful captures, without subtracting refunds. `reversed` is cumulative successful refunds. Refunds do not restore secured funds. Successful void sets `closed` and is not a refund; a terminal void outcome clears `cancellationPending`, while an unknown void leaves it set. No combined payment status or maintained net amount is defined here.

Control proposals enter `/payment/controlRequests` as pending and do not immediately change the selected payee, details, target or locks. Guarantor success applies the recorded proposal; supported refusal or failure outcomes leave that proposed change unapplied and require a reason. Payee changes require unlocked details, a declared recipient and no completed or reserved capture; changing the payee clears recipient approval. Final resolution cannot fall below completed and reserved captures or exceed `limitMinor`; once resolved, the target cannot change to another amount. Instruction acceptance and rejection are mutually exclusive guarantor decisions, with a reason required for rejection. The clause's action library exposes requests and recipient approval; guarantor decision operations belong to the payment instruction.

## Connections

Action `bindings` contain named connections. `on` supports `workflow`, `event`, `channel`, `change`, `embedded`, `collection`, `initialized`, `activated` and `timer`. Workflow connections select an authenticated `party` or `channel` and may declare a `request` pattern. `params` supplies the argument mapping over action defaults; the trigger is not automatically copied into arguments. A false connection `when` skips execution, while a false `parameters.conditions.<action>` rejects it. `before` runs before the action; `after` runs only for `acceptedNew`. `once` defaults to false and, when true, marks the connection fired only after an accepted new result. Embedded and collection sources embed their selected paths unless `embed: false`.

Timer connections require exactly one of an absolute `timestamp` or `afterEvent`. Absolute timestamps are Unix microseconds from zero through 9,007,199,254,740,991. Relative timers require a timestamped source and a positive integer `delayMs` no greater than 9,007,199,254,740; the resulting deadline must remain within the timestamp range. Relative `policy` defaults to `first`, which arms once; `latest` replaces the pending keyed timer on later source events. Absolute timers reject `delayMs` and `policy`. `cancelOn` emits cancellation without resetting the connection's armed flag. Timer requests require the Time runtime, and emission does not itself constitute firing.
